thread:
devon: Wild day 10; storm took out a tree branch and snapped my outdoor ethernet run. Had to jury-rig a temporary feed through the window with a garden cable and duct tape. :dizzy_face: Anyone else maintain outdoor Ethernet or is that just me?

harpreet: Yikes. I run mine through PVC conduit. Duct tape is engineer-adjacent but will do in a pinch.

nina: That sounds terrifying but also very Peak WFH. Is the cable actually rated for outdoor use?

devon: Nope, just repurposed Cat6 box cable from the garage. Wrapped it in a ziplock and tape. Router is on the window sill. Holding so far.

trevor: For temporary fixes, get a short outdoor patch cable and seal connectors with self-fusing silicone tape. Cheap and actually weatherproof-ish.

harpreet: If tree trimming is on the agenda, be careful of the power lines. Also PSA: take a photo for the insurance claim if the branch hit something.

ops-bot: ALERT: Severe weather advisory for devon's area. Stay safe. :warning:

nina: Poll (react): :one: Outdoor-rated cable now, :two: do a proper conduit later, :three: call pro arborist

devon: Voting :one: and :two: 10; want a proper fix but need it working for tonight.

trevor: If you want a quick vendor rec, I have a 10m shielded outdoor Cat6 link I bought last year. Works through window gaps fine.

harpreet: Also, plug your modem into a UPS if you haven't already. Storms = weird power sags.

nina: And maybe move the plant out of the path of falling branches. :seedling:

devon: Plant was heroic, survived with superficial leaf injuries. Will buy outdoor cable tomorrow and schedule a trim. Thanks for the tips and the silicone tape rec.

ops-bot: NOTE: weather-safe checklist pinned in #random by ops-bot. :pushpin:
